pr.title: Refactor average calculation
pr.body: average(values): finite numeric inputs; return their mean, or None for an empty list.

changed_files.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 def average(values):
-    if len(values) == 0:
+    count = len(values)
+    if count < 0:
         return None
-    return sum(values) / len(values)
+    return sum(values) / count

gold_issues.description: The empty-input guard can never be true; averaging an empty list raises ZeroDivisionError.

findings.description: The condition 'if count < 0' is incorrect; count should never be negative as it represents the length of the input list.
The calculation of the average should use 'len(values)' instead of 'count' since 'count' is incorrectly defined.

raw_review.final_response: {"decision":"REQUEST_CHANGES","findings":[{"file":"module.py","line":3,"description":"The condition 'if count < 0' is incorrect; count should never be negative as it represents the length of the input list."},{"file":"module.py","line":5,"description":"The calculation of the average should use 'len(values)' instead of 'count' since 'count' is incorrectly defined."}]}

decisions.rationale: Names the mutated negative-length guard but omits its actual empty-input division-by-zero consequence.
count equals len(values); replacing the denominator with len(values) cannot fix the lost empty guard. This additional denominator allegation is unsupported.

normalization_notes: Reviewed final JSON, submitted body and inline comments together. Merged the same allegation across channels; retained all distinct defect allegations.
